subject: Orion Analytics: west edge service degradation & recommended traffic redirect
messages:
From: Timothy Shah <timothy.shah@orionanalytics.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency + errors from west edge - samples attached

Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in user-facing latency and 5xx rates from calls that route to your west edge (us-west-2) around 07:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to 6.8% and tail latency doubled for our streaming endpoints.

I attached a small sample of request/response headers and stacked traces — this is the first time we've observed this scale of degradation in production. Our traffic is steady; nothing changed on our side. Can your team confirm whether there is an ongoing capacity or routing issue? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Tim

Attachments: orion-request-log-snippet.txt (text, 30 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: timothy.shah@orionanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency + errors from west edge - samples attached

Thanks Tim — acknowledging and looping in infra and runtime leads.

Quick summary for the group:
- External: Orion Analytics reports a sharp latency and 5xx spike for traffic terminating on our west edge (likely us-west-2).
- Impact: increased tail latency, observable throughput drop for affected availability zone(s).
- Customer impact: live user sessions degraded; customer has asked for ETA and mitigation.

Ask: Can infra/routing crew validate AZ health (node evictions, queue depth, network saturation) and propose a short-window mitigation plan (traffic steering / edge redirect) we can enact in the next 30–45 mins? If we redirect, confirm model-variant compatibility and approximate additional latency for clients routed east.

I've prepared a quick exec brief (attached) for leadership if we need to escalate. If we are going to steer traffic, I want an explicit rollback plan and monitoring checklist.

- Marissa

Attachments: exec-brief-draft.pdf (2 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:39:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency + errors from west edge - samples attached

Marissa / team — quick technical dump and immediate mitigation recommendation.

Observations (from control plane + node metrics):
- We saw a coordinated node eviction pattern in us-west-2a starting ~07:40; hosts showed abrupt GPU memory pressure and L3 cache thrashing.
- KV-cache miss rate spiked 5x concurrently; continuous batching queues grew and request timeouts increased.
- No config rollouts in the last 12h; telemetry points to hardware/host-level degradation.

Immediate mitigation (15–30 min):
1) Edge redirect: add a targeted routing rule to steer Orion's origin-tagged traffic away from us-west-2a to us-west-2b and us-east-1 (steering ratio 70/30) using the traffic-policy service.
   - Config: routing-change-plan.txt attached (includes policy id, quick curl example, and required auth scope).
2) Model compatibility: use the same model family but switch requests to the quantized-8 variant in the receiving pools to preserve throughput while slightly increasing per-token latency (~10–20ms).
3) Reduce batch window to 15ms for Orion routes to reduce head-of-line latency while the cache warms.
4) Enable temporary increased prefetch for KV cache for the next 60 minutes.

Risks: cross-region routing will add median latency (~30–70ms) for some request paths and will consume extra egress. We should notify the customer and give an ETA.

I'll post the exact traffic-policy curl in 5 minutes and stand by to enact if Marissa approves.

-Karthik

Attachments: routing-change-plan.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Immediate exec briefing: Orion Analytics incident and proposed traffic steering

Aditya — heads-up and request for brief escalation.

We have a production degradation affecting Orion Analytics traffic anchored in our west edge (us-west-2). Infra indicates host-level evictions causing KV-cache miss cascades and higher 5xx rate. Engineering recommends a targeted traffic steer (70/30 west->east split) and temporary switch to quantized-8 variants in the receiving pools. The recommended plan is non-disruptive but will cause a measurable latency increase for some clients and modest egress cost.

Why this needs exec awareness now:
- Orion is a mid-sized enterprise customer with significant usage and an upcoming renew/expansion conversation.
- The mitigation will be visible to customers (latency bump) and may prompt questions about SLAs and a credit request.
- We may need approval for a one-off customer credit or an expedited capacity burst if steering does not fully stabilise traffic.

Proposed next steps:
1) Approve immediate traffic steering and communicate ETA to Orion (we can do this in 15–30 mins).
2) Open a war room channel and offer a 3pm exec sync/update if there is ongoing impact.
3) Pre-authorise up to a small credit (TBD) if the customer requests.

I attached an exec brief (draft) and a technical plan. If you approve, Karthik will apply the routing change and Sean will coordinate customer comms.

-Marissa

Attachments: exec-brief-draft.pdf, routing-change-plan.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: timothy.shah@orionanalytics.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Action taken: targeted routing applied for Orion traffic — ETA and next steps

Timothy,

Quick update following your report this morning:
- We applied a targeted routing policy at 10:45 PDT that steered Orion-tagged traffic away from the affected AZ into healthy pools (70% us-west-2b, 30% us-east-1).
- We also switched receiving pools to the quantized-8 variant and tightened batching from 40ms to 15ms while caches warm.
- Early telemetry shows error rate back down to ~0.8% and median latency trending toward baseline. We'll continue to monitor for the next 90 minutes and will post a final incident note.

Estimated impacts and asks:
- You may see a 20–60ms median latency bump for some requests as traffic routes cross region boundaries.
- If you see any persistent errors, please share traces. We're keeping a war room open and will follow up with a detailed post-incident note.

As a goodwill gesture given the customer impact, we are prepared to discuss a usage credit if desired — please let us know and we'll route the request.

Thanks for raising this quickly — appreciate the fast trace samples.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: external-status-update.txt
